summary.text: A patient aged 40–45 years at ATT start, born outside the Netherlands, had bilateral posterior uveitis with an unspecific choroidal lesion and vitritis and was treated with six months of four-drug ATT after inadequate response to corticosteroids; uveitis resolved.

Bilateral panuveitis with an edematous optic nerve recurred at 8 years with a high QuantiFERON level and no other signs of active TB, and was treated with isoniazid and oral prednisolone for 4 months with clinical resolution, then subconjunctival triamcinolone injections. A second recurrence at 11 years was treated with mycophenolate mofetil and infliximab.

At the last visit, 20 years after initial presentation, no inflammation or CME was seen in either eye; the patient still used mycophenolate mofetil and topical dexamethasone for the left eye. Visual acuity was 0.02 in the right eye with corneal decompensation due to viral keratitis and 0.2 in the left eye; hypertension was controlled with clonidine.

summary.text: A patient aged 45–50 years at ATT start, born outside the Netherlands, had unilateral posterior non-occlusive retinal vasculitis with CME and after a previous inadequate response to corticosteroids was treated with six months of four-drug ATT, with initial uveitis resolution.

Over 13 years of follow-up after ATT there was no uveitis relapse or recurrent CME and no anti-inflammatory drugs or drops were needed. At the last follow-up there was no inflammation or CME in either eye and visual acuity was 1.00 in both eyes. Topical dorzolamide/timolol was used for open-angle glaucoma unrelated to TBU.

summary.text: A patient aged 50–55 years at ATT start, born outside the Netherlands, had bilateral posterior serpiginous-like choroiditis and, after a previous inadequate response to corticosteroids, received six months of four-drug ATT with corticosteroid treatment, after which the inflammation completely subsided.

Anterior uveitis recurred at 8 years in the right eye and at 15 years in both eyes, with CME during follow-up. Systemic workup found no contributing abnormality except a high QuantiFERON level of 9.89. Treatment was subconjunctival betamethasone twice and topical prednisolone acetate 1% up to six times daily.

At the last follow-up, 18 years after initial presentation, no inflammation or CME was found in either eye; visual acuity was 0.7 in the right eye and 1.0 in the left eye, and topical prednisolone acetate 1% was used once a day in both eyes.

Bilateral intermediate uveitis recurred 6 years after ATT with CME during follow-up; repeated systemic workup found no other cause and no IGRA was performed. Mycophenolate mofetil was given, then adalimumab added for unresolved inflammation, and treatment lasted 5 years until complete resolution.
